{
  "segment_function": "evaluation of Arendt's account of modern science and mediation in relation to human adaptations and earth alienation",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The cumulative effect of mundane adaptations may be to intensify the isolation or alienation of human beings from the earth in its givenness.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "Another possibility is that, even if these adaptations are small-scale and mundane, their cumulative effect might be to intensify the isolation or alien- ation of human beings from the earth in its givenness, cutting people off from a vital source of awareness of their own earthbound limitations, which is nec- essary to keep the activity of world building from running amok.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "applies as a possibility regarding cumulative effects of small-scale and mundane adaptations"
      ],
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "claim": "Modern science interposes humanly made technologies of observation and measurement between humans and the world, cutting them off from reality according to Arendt's stylized account.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "Arendt ’s stylized account of the development of the modern natural sciences seems to suggest something like this: insofar as modern science interposes humanly made technologies of observation and measurement between us and the world, it cuts human beings off from the “reality” to which it promised reliable access.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "based on Arendt's stylized account of the development of modern natural sciences"
      ],
      "confidence": 0.95
    }
  ],
